title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
authors: Jacob Devlin, Ming-Wei Chang, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova

code.title: google-research/bert
code.note: the authors' TensorFlow code and the released checkpoints (repo, about 20 minutes for the README and entry path: modeling.py, create_pretraining_data.py, run_classifier.py)

takeaway: Masked-LM pretraining of a deep bidirectional Transformer encoder plus per-task fine-tuning set SOTA on 11 NLP tasks and made pretrain-then-finetune the default recipe; the encoder lineage lives on in embeddings/retrieval via ModernBERT and Ettin.

kb.n: 2017: BERT is this paper's encoder stack, transplanted to transfer learning; its page runs a toy of the full encoder-decoder.
2025: paired encoders and decoders trained with one recipe (the ModernBERT one); a controlled comparison of the BERT and GPT lineages.
2020: the rival left-to-right lineage scaled; in-context learning replaced per-task heads for generation.
2020: its dense retriever (DPR) is a pair of BERT encoders; retrieval is the encoder's main living habitat.
2021: rotary positions replaced BERT's learned absolute positions in modern encoders (ModernBERT) as well as decoders.
2019: masked-span denoising carried into an encoder-decoder, every task as text to text.
2024: gives a decoder-only LLM bidirectional attention over the prompt, BERT's argument applied inside a decoder.
2020: the same encoder and a [CLS]-style class token, applied to image patches.

verdict: Believe the central claim: masked-LM pretraining of a deep bidirectional encoder beats the same model trained left to right, by margins many standard errors wide, and every later encoder confirmed it. Treat next sentence prediction as unproven (one run, one task outside the noise, reversed by RoBERTa) and the dev-set ablations as single, dev-selected runs.
